page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which assist with vector calculations and neural network instructions.

Benchmark evaluations place the D4s_v4 in the lower-to-middle performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, fall into the bottom 25% tier, with scores of 1410.29 and 3705.66 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 207.14 GB/sec, but uncached large block read speeds drop to 17.74 GB/sec, which is categorized as poor. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression at 23.84 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 9.02 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core testing also yields an average score of 1171.0, while multi-core performance and software compilation tasks remain in the bottom 25%.

This instance does not include local storage, meaning it relies entirely on external network-attached storage, though it is Premium Storage capable. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4s_v4 offers a standard, entry-level resource density for workloads that do not require high-performance computing or massive memory footprints. It is recommended for general-purpose workloads, light web serving, basic database operations, and development or testing environments where moderate single-threaded performance is acceptable and extreme multi-core throughput is not required.
